name: Red Hat Sales Essentials
description: A foundational baseline practice defining the core ontology for enterprise technology sales, encompassing customer value articulation, solution alignment, and sales execution lifecycle management.

focuses.name: Customer Value
focuses.description: The dimension of enterprise sales concerned with understanding customer needs, qualifying business opportunities, and articulating measurable value that connects technology solutions to customer outcomes.

focuses.name: Solution Alignment
focuses.description: The dimension of enterprise sales concerned with matching technical capabilities to customer requirements, demonstrating differentiation against alternatives, and validating solution fit through structured proof activities.

focuses.name: Sales Execution
focuses.description: The dimension of enterprise sales concerned with the operational machinery of selling -- go-to-market strategy execution, deal progression, seller capability development, customer relationship management, post-sale success delivery, and subscription lifecycle management.

narrativeTypes.name: Sales Engagement Journey
narrativeTypes.description: A macro-level lifecycle narrative structure capturing the end-to-end progression of a customer engagement from initial discovery through value delivery and expansion.

narrativeElements.name: Discover
narrativeElements.description: The phase of understanding the customer's world -- their challenges, priorities, technology landscape, and decision-making context.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Begin the narrative by establishing the customer's situation and the seller's investigation of their needs. Describe what was learned about the customer's business and why it matters. Ground the discovery in specific industry or organizational context.

narrativeElements.name: Validate
narrativeElements.description: The phase of confirming that a proposed solution addresses the customer's requirements through technical proof, value quantification, and competitive differentiation.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe how the solution was tested against the customer's real requirements. Include both technical validation and business validation. Show how competitive alternatives were addressed and differentiation was established.

narrativeElements.name: Propose
narrativeElements.description: The phase of presenting a formal commercial recommendation that integrates solution design, value justification, and commercial terms into a coherent business case.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe the formal proposal and how it connected technical solution, business value, and commercial structure. Emphasize how the proposal addressed the customer's specific decision criteria and procurement requirements.

narrativeElements.name: Negotiate
narrativeElements.description: The phase of navigating commercial, legal, and procurement processes to reach mutually acceptable terms, guided by value-based positioning rather than price-based concession.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe the negotiation dynamics and how value-based arguments guided concession strategy. Include the role of champions, executive sponsors, and procurement stakeholders in reaching agreement.

narrativeElements.name: Close
narrativeElements.description: The phase of executing the commercial agreement and transitioning from sales engagement to implementation and post-sale success delivery.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe the closing event and the structured transition to post-sale engagement. Emphasize the handoff as a continuation of the relationship rather than an endpoint.

narrativeElements.name: Expand
narrativeElements.description: The phase where demonstrated value and deepened customer relationship generate expansion opportunities, renewal commitments, and customer advocacy.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe how post-sale success creates the foundation for growth. Include value realization evidence, expansion pathways, and the customer's evolution from buyer to advocate.

narrativeTypes.name: Customer Success Story
narrativeTypes.description: A tactical narrative structure using the STAR (Situation-Task-Action-Result) format for documenting and sharing specific customer value realization experiences.

narrativeElements.name: Situation
narrativeElements.description: The customer's starting context -- their organization, industry, strategic priorities, and the specific challenge or opportunity that prompted the engagement.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Set the scene by describing the customer's business context, technology environment, and the specific challenge they faced. Include enough detail for the audience to relate the situation to their own circumstances.

narrativeElements.name: Task
narrativeElements.description: The specific objective or requirement that the customer and seller collaborated to address, including success criteria and constraints.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Define what needed to be achieved in clear, measurable terms. Include the scope of the challenge, the constraints involved, and the criteria by which success would be judged.

narrativeElements.name: Action
narrativeElements.description: The solution approach, implementation journey, and key decisions made during the engagement, including how challenges were overcome.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe the solution design, implementation approach, and the collaborative work between customer and seller. Include specific products or technologies used, but focus on the approach rather than feature lists.

narrativeElements.name: Result
narrativeElements.description: The measurable business outcomes achieved, including quantified benefits, operational improvements, and strategic impact on the customer's organization.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Present results in specific, quantified terms wherever possible. Include both expected and unexpected benefits. Reference independent validation where available.

narrativeTypes.name: Value Story
narrativeTypes.description: A focused narrative structure for articulating business value from problem identification through solution alignment to measurable outcome delivery.

narrativeElements.name: Problem
narrativeElements.description: The business challenge, pain, or unrealized opportunity that creates the impetus for change, expressed in terms of business impact rather than technical deficiency.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Frame the problem in the customer's business language, not technology terminology. Quantify the cost of the status quo. Make the consequences of inaction vivid and specific to the customer's context.

narrativeElements.name: Solution
narrativeElements.description: The technology-enabled approach that addresses the identified problem, described in terms of capabilities and outcomes rather than product features.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe the solution approach at the level appropriate to the audience. Connect specific capabilities to the problems they solve. Differentiate the approach from alternatives the customer may be considering.

narrativeElements.name: Outcome
narrativeElements.description: The measurable business results delivered or projected from the solution, including financial returns, operational improvements, and strategic advantages.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Present outcomes in terms the audience values most. Use validated data to substantiate claims. Project future value alongside delivered results.

narrativeTypes.name: Competitive Narrative
narrativeTypes.description: A tactical narrative structure for positioning against specific competitive alternatives in customer evaluations.

narrativeElements.name: Challenge
narrativeElements.description: The customer's evaluation context, including the alternatives being considered, the decision criteria in play, and the competitive dynamics shaping the evaluation.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Frame the competitive context from the customer's perspective, not the seller's. Describe what the customer is trying to decide and what criteria matter most. Acknowledge the strengths of alternatives honestly.

narrativeElements.name: Alternative
narrativeElements.description: A fair characterization of the competitive alternative being evaluated, including its genuine strengths and the specific areas where it falls short of the customer's requirements.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe the competitor's approach and where it works well. Then identify specific gaps, limitations, or risks relevant to this customer's requirements and decision criteria.

narrativeElements.name: Advantage
narrativeElements.description: The specific ways the seller's approach better addresses the customer's requirements, decision criteria, and strategic direction, supported by evidence and proof points.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Connect each advantage directly to a customer decision criterion or requirement. Support each claim with evidence. Emphasize long-term strategic advantages alongside immediate technical benefits.

narrativeTypes.name: Citation Standard
narrativeTypes.description: A reference documentation structure for attributing sources, evidence, and intellectual contributions used in practice documentation.

narrativeElements.name: Author
narrativeElements.description: The individual or organization responsible for creating the cited work.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Provide the full name of the author or authoring organization. For organizational authors, use the formal organization name.

narrativeElements.name: Date
narrativeElements.description: The publication or release date of the cited work.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Provide the year of publication. For web resources that are regularly updated, use the most recent access or update date.

narrativeElements.name: Title
narrativeElements.description: The title of the cited work.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Provide the complete title as it appears on the published work. Do not abbreviate or paraphrase.

narrativeElements.name: Source
narrativeElements.description: The publication venue, URL, or retrieval information for the cited work.
narrativeElements.howToUse: For web resources, provide the URL. For published works, provide the publisher and publication venue. For internal documents, note the internal classification.

competencies.name: Customer Discovery
competencies.description: The ability to research, engage, and systematically uncover customer challenges, priorities, requirements, and decision-making context through structured questioning and active listening.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands the purpose of customer discovery and can conduct basic research on prospect organizations using public sources. Can follow prepared discovery scripts and talk tracks in initial customer conversations.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Conducts structured discovery conversations that uncover customer challenges and connect them to potential solutions with moderate coaching support. Prepares call plans with relevant background research and targeted questions.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Independently leads multi-stakeholder discovery sessions that uncover strategic priorities, hidden pain, and decision dynamics without relying on prescribed scripts. Identifies needs that customers have not yet articulated.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Designs discovery approaches for complex enterprise situations involving multiple business units, competing stakeholders, and ambiguous requirements. Mentors others on discovery technique and provides actionable coaching.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Creates new discovery frameworks and methodologies that improve the organization's ability to understand customer needs at scale. Recognized as an authority on enterprise customer engagement and needs assessment.

competencies.name: Value Articulation
competencies.description: The ability to construct, quantify, and communicate business value arguments that connect technology solutions to measurable customer outcomes, from qualitative themes through financial modeling to realized value tracking.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands standard value themes and can articulate basic value messaging using prepared materials and sales play content. Can reference customer success stories and case studies in value conversations.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Constructs customer-specific value hypotheses aligned to customer priorities using standard value frameworks and assessment methodologies. Uses value assessment tools to generate quantified business impact estimates.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Independently constructs and presents quantified value arguments customized to each customer's specific financial and strategic context. Incorporates third-party validation into value presentations. Effectively presents value at the executive level.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Develops custom financial models and executive-level business cases for complex, multi-product engagements. Trains other sellers on value articulation techniques and provides real-time coaching during customer engagements.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Shapes the organization's value selling methodology and measurement strategy at a strategic level. Creates new approaches to value quantification and communication that become organizational standards.

competencies.name: Technical Positioning
competencies.description: The ability to translate technology capabilities into customer-relevant solution architectures, demonstrate technical fit through structured validation, and bridge the gap between technical features and business outcomes.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands the product portfolio at a summary level and can identify basic product-to-requirement mappings for common customer scenarios. Can navigate demonstration environments and deliver pre-configured demonstrations.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Designs standard solution architectures for common customer scenarios and delivers intermediate-depth technical presentations. Understands integration requirements and can identify standard integration patterns.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Independently designs complex solution architectures addressing multi-dimensional customer requirements. Delivers deep technical sessions with hands-on demonstrations customized for each customer's specific environment.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Recognized as a technical authority capable of designing innovative architectures for complex enterprise scenarios. Mentors other technical sellers on solution design techniques and contributes to reference architecture development.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Defines technical solution design standards and reference architectures for the organization. Drives innovation in pre-sales technical engagement approaches and shapes the organization's technical selling methodology.

competencies.name: Competitive Intelligence
competencies.description: The ability to gather, analyze, contextualize, and deploy competitive market intelligence to inform sales positioning, strategy, and customer conversations.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Can locate and use standardized competitive comparison materials for known competitors in the most common competitive scenarios. Understands fundamental differentiators of the open source, subscription-based approach.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Uses competitive intelligence assets effectively in customer conversations. Follows competitive intelligence updates for current market positioning. Can contextualize competitive positioning for specific customer situations.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Synthesizes competitive intelligence dynamically in customer conversations rather than reciting from prepared materials. Identifies and capitalizes on time-sensitive competitive opportunities. Handles competitive objections with evidence-based responses.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Develops competitive strategy and positioning for specific market segments or customer verticals. Creates or significantly improves competitive intelligence assets based on field experience and market analysis. Mentors others on competitive positioning techniques.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Defines the organization's competitive intelligence strategy and methodology at an organizational level. Drives innovation in competitive intelligence gathering, analysis, and deployment. Shapes organizational response to major competitive market shifts.

competencies.name: Deal Orchestration
competencies.description: The discipline of progressing sales opportunities through qualification stages, managing commercial transactions, coordinating cross-functional team engagement, and navigating complex enterprise procurement processes.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands qualification methodology terminology and progressive evidence requirements per sales stage. Can enter and maintain basic opportunity information in the pipeline management system.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Applies the qualification framework to assess opportunities with coaching support. Manages pipeline hygiene with accurate stage assignment and forecasting. Can structure basic commercial proposals for standard engagement scenarios.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Rigorously applies qualification methodology across the entire sales cycle. Accurately forecasts deal outcomes and timing based on multi-dimensional qualification assessment. Expertly structures complex commercial proposals.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Develops creative qualification and deal strategies for complex enterprise engagements. Leads pipeline reviews and coaches other sellers on qualification improvement and deal structuring. Manages strategic commercial negotiations at the executive level.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Defines and evolves the organization's opportunity management and deal execution methodology. Integrates qualification and pipeline management with emerging analytics and intelligence capabilities. Drives organizational pipeline discipline and commercial innovation.

competencies.name: Relationship Building
competencies.description: The ability to build, deepen, and sustain trusted advisory relationships with customers and partners across multiple stakeholder levels, from initial rapport through strategic partnership.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands the importance of relationship-based selling and the distinction between transactional and consultative engagement. Can build initial rapport with customer contacts and maintain professional communication cadence.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Builds productive working relationships across customer business and technical functions. Applies structured techniques for establishing credibility and trust. Manages basic multi-stakeholder communication and coordination.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Consistently operates as a trusted advisor where customers actively seek perspective on decisions beyond immediate transactions. Successfully navigates complex multi-stakeholder relationships. Manages executive-level relationships with strategic engagement planning.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Builds strategic partnerships that survive personnel changes and organizational shifts. Mentors others on relationship-building techniques and provides coaching on complex relationship dynamics. Creates innovative approaches to executive access.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Defines the organization's approach to customer relationship management and strategic partnership development. Creates frameworks for measuring and developing relationship quality at organizational scale.

competencies.name: Customer Success Management
competencies.description: The ability to ensure customers realize value from purchased technology through proactive engagement, technical guidance, business outcome tracking, and strategic partnership development during the post-sale phase.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands the post-sale engagement model and the complementary roles of technical success and business relationship management. Can conduct basic customer meetings covering operational status and open issues.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Manages customer engagement cadence effectively with regular meetings, periodic reports, and proactive communication. Conducts architecture health checks and provides improvement recommendations. Uses value tracking tools.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Drives measurable customer outcomes aligned to pre-sale value commitments. Conducts strategic and operational planning sessions with customers. Provides product roadmap influence through structured customer feedback.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Achieves industry-benchmark outcomes in customer productivity, operational efficiency, and return on investment. Develops best practices for customer success that are adopted organizationally. Creates compelling customer success stories.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Defines and evolves the organization's customer success methodology and engagement model. Drives innovation in customer success measurement, value realization tracking, and customer advocacy development.

competencies.name: Sales Enablement
competencies.description: The ability to design, develop, and deliver training programs, content assets, credentialing pathways, and tools that improve the effectiveness of sales and technical sales professionals.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands the enablement content ecosystem including content platforms, depth-level taxonomy, and content types. Can identify training needs based on seller performance gaps.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Develops role-specific training content for sellers and technical sellers. Curates and organizes content with appropriate classification and tagging. Designs assessment tools for skill evaluation.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Designs comprehensive enablement programs covering multiple competency areas and seller profiles. Develops partner enablement modules across sales, technical sales, and implementation tracks. Integrates technology tools into enablement programs.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Designs organizational enablement strategy spanning internal and partner audiences. Creates innovative enablement approaches including skills networks, credentialing programs, and digital badges. Drives adoption of AI-powered coaching tools.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Defines the organization's sales enablement philosophy and methodology. Drives innovation in sales training and development approaches. Recognized as an authority on sales enablement in enterprise technology.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise technology sales organizations manage complex pipelines where opportunities arrive from diverse sources -- prospecting, inbound inquiries, partner referrals, and digital engagement signals. The challenge lies not merely in identifying opportunities but in applying sufficient qualification rigor to ensure that organizational investment flows toward engagements with genuine commercial potential.

The opportunity must progress through a disciplined qualification framework that systematically validates business need, buyer authority, solution fit, competitive positioning, and commercial viability. Each stage transition requires the accumulation of specific evidence that intensifies as the opportunity advances.

Qualification begins with structured discovery that identifies quantifiable business outcomes, economic buyer authority, and the consequences of customer inaction. Technical validation confirms solution fit through demonstrations and proof-of-concept activities, while value articulation quantifies the business case using structured assessment tools. The identification and development of a customer champion accelerates the commercial decision process.

The qualified opportunity reaches commercial commitment with a comprehensive evidence base: validated business need, confirmed solution fit, quantified value proposition, identified champion, and mapped decision process. The expansion stage demonstrates that effective opportunity management creates a virtuous cycle where demonstrated value generates follow-on opportunities, transforming individual transactions into sustained growth engines.

narrativeContexts.context: Understanding a customer begins well before the first conversation. Research into the organization's industry dynamics, competitive pressures, and technology landscape builds the foundation for relevant engagement. Initial targeting identifies organizations whose challenges align with available solution capabilities.

Validation of customer understanding occurs through active dialogue with multiple stakeholders across business and technical functions. Discovery conversations test and refine initial hypotheses about the customer's challenges and priorities.

As understanding deepens, the engagement shifts from information gathering to value creation. The seller demonstrates relevance through tailored presentations, demonstrations, and reference sharing that connect available capabilities to the customer's specific challenges.

Building trust requires consistent delivery of insight and value that transcends individual transactions. The customer begins to seek the seller's perspective on strategic technology decisions, signaling a shift from vendor to trusted advisor.

The trusting relationship manifests in concrete commercial outcomes -- active subscriptions, deployed technology, and measurable business impact. Post-sale engagement deepens the relationship through dedicated success resources and collaborative optimization.

The highest state of customer progression sees the customer actively championing the seller's solutions in the market. Through peer-to-peer programs, published case studies, and organic recommendation, the customer becomes a market-making advocate whose endorsement creates a virtuous cycle that generates new opportunities.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise technology buyers rarely evaluate a single vendor in isolation. Most significant decisions involve comparison against proprietary platform vendors, cloud-native services, other open source providers, and internal solutions. Effective competitive positioning requires understanding not just what competitors offer but what the customer actually values.

Proprietary platform alternatives offer integrated, vertically optimized solutions that appeal to organizations seeking simplicity. Cloud-native alternatives offer convenience and elastic scalability but introduce platform dependency. Each alternative has genuine strengths, and effective competitive positioning acknowledges these honestly.

The open source, subscription-based approach provides structural competitive advantages that strengthen with adoption scale: architectural flexibility through open standards, community-driven innovation, predictable subscription economics, and multi-cloud deployment consistency. These advantages are substantiated through competitive battlecards, benchmark comparisons, and peer customer references.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise technology sales begins with the disciplined work of understanding a customer's world before proposing solutions. Structured discovery conversations, guided by consultative selling skills, transform initial meetings from product presentations into collaborative explorations of business challenges. The discovery phase produces documented understanding that informs every subsequent engagement decision.

Validation transforms hypotheses into evidence. Technical validation confirms solution architectures meet requirements through demonstrations and proof-of-concept engagements. Business validation quantifies expected impact using structured assessment tools. Competitive validation establishes differentiation through evidence-based positioning. Independent analyst studies documenting returns of 379-386% illustrate the magnitude of value effective validation can substantiate.

The formal proposal integrates validated solution design, quantified business value, and commercial structure into a coherent business case. The subscription model provides flexibility through multiple purchasing options, support tiers, and term structures. The champion is equipped with validated evidence to advocate through internal approval processes.

Commercial negotiation guided by value-based positioning preserves deal integrity while demonstrating flexibility. Negotiation positions are grounded in quantified business outcomes, shifting conversation from price comparison to value comparison. Creative commercial structuring addresses customer concerns while sustaining deal value.

Contract execution marks the beginning of a partnership. Structured handoff transfers full engagement context to post-sale success resources. Technical and business success resources are assigned, establishing the framework for value realization that will sustain the relationship through renewal and expansion cycles.

Expansion emerges from demonstrated value and deepened trust. Post-deployment metrics confirm pre-sale commitments. Architecture health checks identify optimization opportunities. At its peak, the engagement produces customer advocacy -- peer-to-peer sharing, published success stories, and organic recommendation -- that creates market impact extending far beyond the individual account.
